summary: No restricted grammar: both 'likely' flags and all four 'review' flags are tool errors. The text has several small stumbles rather than blocking faults: a dangling 'het' after 'regel', a 'Ze' that switches referent from people to laws, generic 'je' where Harry addresses McGonagall ('Dan moet je een god zijn'), and the 'kunt u niet doen' calque. Five glosses are spent on known words while brein, knipperde and planeten go unglossed.

findings.fragment: Een menselijke geest kan zich niet zomaar de hele anatomie van een kat voorstellen, en, en al die kattenbiochemie, en hoe zit het met de neurologie?
findings.problem: The verbal frame holds 9 words between 'kan' and 'voorstellen', and the stammered list continues after the closing verb.
findings.required_fix: Close the frame early and hang the list on a colon: 'Een menselijke \gl{geest}{mind} kan zich dat niet zomaar voorstellen: de hele anatomie van een kat, en, en al die kattenbiochemie, en hoe zit het met de \emph{neurologie}?'

findings.fragment: Dat is niet zomaar een willekeurige regel, het volgt uit de vorm van de kwantum-Hamiltoniaan!
findings.problem: 'het' has no het-word to refer to ('regel' is a de-word), so the pronoun dangles and the comma splice reads as a run-on.
findings.evidence: EN: 'it's implied by …' (it = the rule) vs NL: 'het volgt uit' after 'een willekeurige regel'
findings.required_fix: Use the demonstrative and a semicolon, as V1: 'Dat is niet zomaar een willekeurige regel; die volgt uit de vorm van de kwantum-Hamiltoniaan!'

findings.fragment: Ze hadden de vorm van simpele wiskunde, en de kleinste deeltjes volgden die wiskunde.
findings.problem: 'Ze' switches referent: in the two previous sentences 'Ze' is 'mensen' ('Ze ontdekten', 'Ze leerden'); here it must be 'de wetten'. The reader re-parses.
findings.evidence: sequence 'Ze ontdekten: … Ze leerden: … Ze hadden de vorm …' in b032
findings.required_fix: Repeat the noun: 'De wetten hadden de vorm van simpele wiskunde, en de kleinste deeltjes volgden die wiskunde.'

findings.fragment: Dan moet je een god zijn!
findings.problem: Harry is talking to McGonagall, who answers 'Zo heeft nog nooit iemand me genoemd'; generic 'je' means nobody has called her anything, and it breaks the u-address fixed in the bible.
findings.evidence: glossary.json: Harry addresses McGonagall with 'u'; b031 reply presupposes that she was called a god
findings.required_fix: 'Dan moet u een god zijn!' (as V1 and V3). The generic 'je' in 'Als je die regel loslaat … dan krijg je' may stay.

findings.problem: Word-for-word 'You can't do that'; in Dutch 'Dat kunt u niet doen' reads first as a moral prohibition (you mustn't), not as 'that is impossible', and the emphasis on 'doen' strengthens that reading.
findings.evidence: EN: 'You can't do that!' (impossibility, cf. b028) vs NL: 'Dat kunt u niet doen!' (prohibition)
findings.required_fix: Drop 'doen' and move the emphasis to the modal: '“\emph{Dat \emph{kunt} u niet!}”' (as V3).

findings.problem: 'brein' is not in any lexicon list and occurs five times unglossed (once inside 'kattenbrein'); it carries the mind = brain point of b032.
findings.evidence: vocab rows brein (unknown, n=4, b032) and kattenbrein (unknown, b028), action review
findings.required_fix: Gloss at the first occurrence: 'met een \gl{kattenbrein}{cat brain}'; the bare 'brein' in b032 is then understood. Lexicon owner: add 'brein' as a transparent cognate.

findings.fragment: Professor Anderling knipperde met haar ogen.
findings.problem: 'knipperen' is unknown and unglossed; 'met haar ogen' narrows it to an eye movement but does not give the meaning.
findings.evidence: vocab row knipperen: unknown, action review; V1 and V3 gloss it

findings.fragment: de muziek van de planeten was dezelfde melodie als de val van een appel
findings.problem: 'planeet' is hard (B2) and unglossed; together with 'melodie' (B1) it makes a two-new-word sentence.
findings.evidence: lexicon planeet hard (B2), action replace-or-gloss; cluster b032 (sentence): melodie, planeet
findings.required_fix: No plain equivalent for 'planeten' ('sterren' changes the meaning): gloss it and replace 'melodie': 'de muziek van de \gl{planeten}{planets} was hetzelfde liedje als de val van een appel.'

findings.problem: Four unglossed B1 words against a stretch budget of 3.
findings.evidence: lexicon stretch (B1): gestreept (b025, tool lemmatised as 'streepen'), loslaten (b028, tool lemmatised as 'loslaan'), melodie (b032), steun (b024); budget 3
findings.required_fix: 'de kleine gestreepte kat' → 'de kleine kat met strepen'; 'melodie' → 'liedje' (L8). 'loslaat' and 'steun' then fit the budget.

findings.problem: Five of the thirteen glosses sit on words the reader knows; the slots are needed for L6, L7, L8.
findings.evidence: lexicon: aarzelen A2, stapel A2, stoot A2 (diminutive; 'ademde in korte, snelle stootjes' explains itself), willekeurig A2, uitzondering known (B1 path word)
findings.required_fix: Drop these five glosses (b022 aarzelde; b024 stapel; b026 stootjes; b028 willekeurige; b032 uitzondering) and remove them from @glosses.

findings.problem: 'wazig' is unknown and needs a gloss, while the known noun 'waas' says the same thing without one.
findings.evidence: vocab row wazig: unknown, glossed; lexicon waas: known A2 (haze, mist)
findings.required_fix: 'Er kwam een waas voor Harry’s ogen.' (as V3) and drop the gloss.

findings.problem: A bare comparative as a one-word opener is terse to the point of oddness in speech.
Understandable but stiff; 'tot zover' normally takes a bare noun ('tot zover de theorie').
findings.evidence: V1 'en weg was dat allemaal', V3 'en daar ging dat allemaal' are the idiomatic turns
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'En toen veranderde een vrouw in een kat, en weg was dat allemaal.'

findings.fragment: kwantum-Hamiltoniaan, unitariteit, FTL-signalen, anatomie, kattenbiochemie, neurologie, neuronen
findings.problem: Flagged as unknown and as clusters, but they are deliberate opaque jargon (the set-up for 'Magie.'), nearly all transparent cognates. Only 'FTL' is opaque even to an English reader.
findings.evidence: vocab rows unknown, action review; clusters b028 (anatomie, kattenbiochemie, neurologie), (loslaan, unitariteit), b032 (brein, neuron); translator @notes and bible
findings.required_fix: No change; do not gloss. Optional: 'FTL-signalen' → 'signalen sneller dan het licht' spells the abbreviation out at no cost. Lexicon owner: mark the jargon so it stops counting toward density and clusters.

findings.problem: Tool-unknown but fine: 'universum' is a cognate, 'dát' is 'dat' with an emphasis accent.
findings.evidence: vocab rows universum, dát: unknown; cluster b032 (dát, universum) is an artefact
findings.required_fix: No change. Lexicon owner: add 'universum'; tool: normalise accented 'dát' to 'dat'.

findings.problem: Hard (B2) word, but precise and already glossed; the plain alternatives lose the sense of sincere.

findings.fragment: Het hele idee van één universum met wiskundig regelmatige wetten, dát spoelde net weg door de wc; het hele idee van de \emph{natuurkunde}.
findings.problem: Left-dislocated topic with a resumptive demonstrative; at 21 words with a single modifier and the accent on 'dát' it stays readable (the V1 and V3 versions of this sentence are heavier).
findings.required_fix: Keep. If shortened anyway: 'Het hele idee van één universum met wiskundig regelmatige wetten — dát spoelde net door de wc. Het hele idee van \emph{natuurkunde}.'

flag_decisions.reason: Plain attributive adjective ('gestreept', B1 in the lexicon) with no complements; a vocabulary question, handled in L9.

'klinken' is a copula, not an auxiliary; 'verstikt' is a predicative adjective describing a state (look-alike table: 'zijn' + adjectival participle). No 'worden', no agent. The identical sentence was not flagged in V1 or V3.
Perfectum with zijn of the intransitive 'veranderen in' (A-PERF); no agent, no 'worden'.

flag_decisions.span: , dát spoelde net weg door de wc
flag_decisions.reason: Resumptive demonstrative (the accent marks it as such) after a left-dislocated topic, finite verb in second position: a main clause, not a relative clause.
Demonstrative subject with V2 order ('dat was') in the apposition 'een brein, dat was een mens'; a relative clause would be verb-final ('dat een mens was').
'dat' is a determiner in the noun phrase 'dat alles' (all that); no finite verb follows, so there is no complement clause.

flag_decisions.span: kan zich niet zomaar de hele anatomie van een kat voorstellen
flag_decisions.reason: Nine words inside the frame and the list continues after 'voorstellen'; see L1.

tool_feedback.reason: 'klinken' (and 'lijken', 'blijven', 'voelen') + participle is a copula + predicative adjective, never a passive; also the same sentence passed unflagged in V1 and V3, so the rule fires inconsistently.
'dat' is a determiner before 'alles' and no finite verb follows; R-DAT should require a clause (finite verb after 'dat').
'stootjes' is the diminutive plural of 'stoot' (A2, in the lexicon); the lemmatiser produced the non-word 'stoo'.
'loslaat' is a form of 'loslaten' (B1, in the lexicon); the lemmatiser produced the non-word 'loslaan'. The word is stretch, not unknown.
'gestreepte' is the adjective 'gestreept' (B1, in the lexicon), not a verb 'streepen'.

tool_feedback.ref: vocab: dát (+ cluster b032 dát, universum)
tool_feedback.reason: Emphasis accent on 'dat' (A1); strip acute accents before lookup.

tool_feedback.ref: vocab: kwantum-hamiltoniaan, unitariteit, anatomie, kattenbiochemie, neurologie, kattenbrein, neuron (+ clusters b028)
tool_feedback.reason: Deliberate opaque jargon per the bible; a per-scene jargon list would keep these out of density, known-share and cluster verdicts. Compound splitting (kat + biochemie, kat + brein) would also help.
Not listed at all (treated as a proper noun?), yet 'FTL' is an opaque abbreviation; abbreviations should at least surface as unknown.
Transparent cognates absent from every list; add to the lexicon.
Glosses on aarzelde, stapel, stootjes, willekeurige, uitzondering (all known) are not reported; a 'gloss on known word' row would catch gloss bloat.
A single participle used attributively right before a noun, without complements, is an adjective.
Pronoun immediately followed by the finite verb is a demonstrative main clause, as the tool's own note suspects; auto-dismiss or lower confidence below 0.3.
